rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-064 (illustrative figures), A-17: some operators win blocks at prices below their own value for them, with the cap holding the clearing price at the third-highest bidder's value, so the cap of two blocks keeps the operators from holding a third block they would value above its price.

No matching assumption in WE-064; judged from the text: the TCA awards the blocks itself and consents to every transfer (reg. 14), so awards above two blocks to one person and its affiliates can be refused.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-064 (illustrative figures), A-5: some bidders or holders use stakes or joint ventures below the affiliate line (control of more than 50%), so some holdings above two blocks go uncounted.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-064 (illustrative figures), A-13: licensees, entrants and town councils can organize to lobby at a cost below their stakes.

No matching assumption in WE-064; judged from the text: licenses run 15 years to 31 December 2042 with the cap binding every later holder, so holders of blocks expect the cap to stay for the term; renewal is open (re-auction or renewal at market value).

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-064 (illustrative figures), A-10: after the auction some licensees value their licenses less than others would (an entrant cannot finance the build-out, or values change).

No matching assumption in WE-064; judged from the text: transfer needs the Authority's consent (reg. 14) and may be barred before 2032 under U1-b, so rights are not freely tradable, though a transfer is possible; the text says nothing on the cost of a transfer.

No matching assumption in WE-064; judged from the text: the TCA's added costs (M9 million for the auction, M2 million a year for monitoring) are funded by an increase in its annual appropriation from the general budget.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-064 (illustrative figures), A-17: some operators win blocks at prices below their own value for them (the cap holds the clearing price at the third-highest bidder's value).
